To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
American Indians with type II diabetes prefer mental health services that include traditional healing and that they prefer providers who have a Native background.
American Indian adults living on reservation lands, those with anxiety, those who engaged in spiritual activities, and those with past health care discrimination, preferred traditional services.
American Indian participants with type 2 Diabetes Mellitus preferred mental health services and providers that were culturally relevant to their lives.
